question.prompt: The inequality \(x^2-2x+m>0\) holds for every real number \(x\). The discriminant must be less than 0. What is the discriminant when \(m=2\)?

solutions.explanation: The discriminant is \(4-8=-4\), which is less than 0. The parabola opens upward, so the expression is indeed always positive in this case.
solutions.title: Calculate the discriminant
